name: Hassenuah
overview: Hassenuah was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, as explicitly noted in 1 Chronicles 9:7. He is identified primarily by his tribal affiliation and his lineage within Israel. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited information about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Hassenuah means 'the hated one,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a negative connotation. This name was not given by God but is recorded in the biblical text, offering insight into the possible character or experiences associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Hassenuah is identified as the son of Hodaviah, an inferred relationship based on the biblical record in 1 Chronicles 9:7. His primary family connection is to his father and his ancestral tribe of Benjamin, with no further familial details provided.
scriptureSignificance: Hassenuah's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Benjamin, which helps establish the continuity and preservation of the tribe after the exile. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:7 contributes to the biblical emphasis on maintaining the identity and heritage of God's people through their descendants. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving His chosen lineage.
